architecture: One orchestrator, one page audit engine, one cache service, one bounded repair pass, one portfolio citation/backlink control plane, and one post-publish distribution observation chain.

severity_policy.hard_fail: Only corruption, unsafe publication, false evidence, wrong-domain routing, secret exposure, broken required journeys, nondeterministic governed output, or executable failure.
severity_policy.strong_warning: Repairable page defects, administrative drift, or a quality issue needing attention. Never blocks by itself.
severity_policy.soft_warning: Word-count targets, optional metadata, cadence variance, low cache hit rate, and editorial preferences.
severity_policy.self_repair: Generated daily pages receive one deterministic mechanical repair pass and one final audit. No recursive repair loops.

json.rationale: Malformed JSON is corruption; every downstream registry reads it.

workflow_trace.rationale: Workflow safety: a broken trace means release automation cannot be reasoned about.

pages_changed.rationale: Unsafe publication: page audit over changed output.

pages_release.rationale: Unsafe publication: page audit over release output.

pages_full.rationale: Unsafe publication: full page audit. Self-reports hard/strong/soft counts.

deterministic_build.rationale: Nondeterministic governed output, named verbatim in severity_policy.

hostile.rationale: Unsafe publication; already separates advisory fit notes from failures.

links.rationale: Broken required journeys and wrong-domain routing.

citation_contract.rationale: False evidence in the citation control plane.

portfolio_backlinks.rationale: Wrong-domain routing and affiliation-disclosure integrity across 476 published backlinks.

backlink_local.rationale: False evidence: verifies each published backlink actually resolves.

cache_self_test.rationale: Cache corruption would serve wrong bytes for governed output.

recovery_agency.rationale: Backfill and self-heal accounting is administrative drift; a gap is repairable and does not make published output wrong.

distribution_chain.rationale: Post-publish observation. Passes today with 0 verified citations, so it measures reach rather than correctness, and depends on secrets that are absent in local runs.

social_contract.rationale: Declares missing_secrets_nonblocking_by_default and strict_social_failure_opt_in - non-blocking by its own contract.

content_pattern.rationale: A page that carries no direct answer, no query-bearing h1, an empty table cell, or no outbound editorial link cannot be quoted by an answer engine or returns nothing when it is. All four checks measure 100% across the 495 published pages, so blocking cannot regress a clean surface.

published_tree_purity.why: sites/ is publicly fetchable and every AI crawler is allowed; an operator surface there discloses network operations regardless of its noindex meta.

external_sources.rationale: False evidence. These publications now cite 34 outside domains, and the whole value of that is that the citations are real. This check fails if a registered source has no verification receipt, if its last fetch was not a 200, or if a citation's host disagrees with its registered domain. A fabricated government URL on a publication whose only asset is credibility is the worst failure available here, so it blocks. The network fetch is a separate opt-in flag; the blocking run is structural and offline.

click_depth.rationale: Broken required journeys. Orphan count correlates inversely with AI citations across the 9 measured properties: the most-cited property carries 3 orphans and every zero-citation property is heavily orphaned. All three publications currently measure 0 orphans at a maximum depth of 2, so blocking cannot regress a clean surface - it only stops the daily generator from silently reintroducing pages nothing links to.

nav_rebuild_after_publish.rationale: Broken required journeys, and the one shape of that this gate could not see. build_site_navigation.py renders bounded navigation blocks - twelve siblings, twelve recent pages - and 3ce3dbb gave it an assertion that refused to write any page that lost a link. A bounded window over a growing library has to evict, so from the day both landed, every autopilot run that actually published something aborted the rebuild and left the new pages orphaned; run 33101813017 on 2026-08-27 is the first. Neither script is wrong alone and both pass on the committed tree, which is exactly why nothing here caught it: no check ran the workflow's own order, publish then rebuild. This one does, against a temporary copy with a synthetic new daily page in it, and requires the rebuild to complete, no eviction to leave a page unreached, and click depth to still measure zero orphans. It also fails if the fixture stops evicting anything, because a guard that no longer exercises its case is not a guard.

analytics_separation.rationale: Wrong-domain routing: a placeholder, missing, shared or cross-publication analytics id sends one publication's reader data into another's project.

cadence_gate_integrity.rationale: A gate that cannot hold a verdict is false evidence about whether publishing is governed at all. cadence_gate.js used to rewrite the ledger it reads, so a blocked run cleared itself on the next invocation - observed as BLOCKED then CLEAR with nothing changed between them. That made the weekly publishing cap unenforceable while still reporting a status, which is worse than having no cap, because the green run was taken as proof. This blocks on the gate mutating its ledger, on two identical runs disagreeing, on no workflow invoking the gate, and on CI being able to run the acceptance path.

autopilot_cadence_cap.rationale: False evidence about whether publishing is governed. data/cadence/policy.json declared 3 new pages per week and scripts/cadence_gate.js enforced it, while the autopilot published 9 a day - 63 a week, 21x the cap - and never met the gate, because git-auto-commit-action pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN and GitHub does not trigger workflows on those pushes. The cap was written down, validated, and structurally unreachable by the only process that could break it. This blocks if the generator stops consulting the declared allowance, applies it after generating rather than before, lets it exceed the cap, or stops reporting a zero-page day as the ordinary success it is.

severity_matrix_policy.note: A validator absent from severity_matrix is treated as HARD_FAIL. Failing safe matters more than convenience: an unclassified check is one nobody has reasoned about.
severity_matrix_policy.strict_flag: --strict promotes STRONG_WARNING and SOFT_WARNING failures to blocking.
